claims.explanation: U-18666A inhibits oxidosqualene cyclase and disrupts lysosomal cholesterol transport, likely causing selective toxicity in cancer cells with high cholesterol uptake and lysosomal dependency. Sensitizing features include mutations in cholesterol trafficking genes (NPC1, NPC2) and high expression of LDLR, while protective features include low cholesterol synthesis and high efflux capacity.

features.basis: U-18666A targets NPC1 pathway; mutations may impair cholesterol egress, enhancing drug effect
NPC2 binds cholesterol; loss may exacerbate lysosomal cholesterol accumulation
High LDLR increases cholesterol uptake, promoting lysosomal overload
ACAT1 esterifies cholesterol, reducing free cholesterol toxicity
Cholesterol efflux reduces lysosomal accumulation
Cholesterol efflux reduces lysosomal accumulation
High SQLE may bypass oxidosqualene cyclase inhibition
Upregulated cholesterol synthesis may compensate for inhibition
TP53 mutations common in sensitive lines; may impair stress response
PIK3CA mutations frequent in sensitive lines; may alter lipid metabolism
KRAS mutations common in sensitive lines; may increase cholesterol uptake
PTEN loss in sensitive lines; may activate PI3K/AKT and lipid synthesis
